title: Rally
description: Rally mechanics: joining or starting group attacks on bosses/players.
sources: Kingshot community guide (Rally Principles for Everyone)

entries.name: Rally Principles for Everyone
entries.summary: Which hero skills count when hosting versus joining a rally, how member bonuses are selected, why stacking the same hero matters, and where to view rally bonuses.

hosting_skills.note: When you host a rally, all three expedition skills from your (rally leader) hero are used.

skills.name: Damage Taken Chance Down
skills.effect: Reduces the chance of taking damage.

skills.name: Lethality Up
skills.effect: Boosts lethality, making attacks more effective.

joining_rules: When you join a rally, only your rally leader hero counts for the rally bonus.
The first hero is your rally leader; creating troop formations is the key to success.

member_bonus_selection.question: When joining a rally, which chief heroes count for the Rally Member bonus?
answers: The heroes with the highest expedition skill (5*).
stacking_examples: If everyone uses Chenko in Bear Hunt rallies they stack: 4x DMG Up 25%.
In King's Castle everyone uses Gordon: 4x Health Up 25%.

how_to_view_bonuses: Open the War > Rally screen to check details.
Click the info button to see the rally leader's hero skills.
The info button also shows the top 4 heroes of rally members.

entries.name: What a rally joiner actually contributes
entries.summary: In many important rally situations, a joiner does NOT contribute their entire personal stat sheet the way players casually assume (only the rally-leader hero counts for the member bonus — see rally-principles). So a joiner who blindly chases deeper governor gear, charms and combat stats can spend a lot while improving real rally impact less than a better-organized player.

joiners_overvalue: deep personal stat upgrades with weak practical rally impact
cosmetic power jumps that don't improve real contribution
building like a rally captain while mostly playing as a joiner
details.principle: Role identity comes before upgrade priority: if you are a joiner, build like a joiner. A rally joiner is not a weaker captain — it is a different job.
details.note: This is a practical/organizational claim from a community guide; the exact per-rally stat contribution formula is not specified. See rally-principles for the confirmed 'only rally-leader hero counts when joining' mechanic.
details.source: kingshotguide.com Rally Joiner Mechanics guide, shared by user (2026-03-21)

entries.name: Rally member (help) bonus: 4-hero cap and displacement
entries.summary: The rally member 'help' bonus stacks from at most 4 heroes — 4x is the maximum the game counts. The game auto-selects the 4 STRONGEST member heroes, so a stronger hero with the WRONG buff type can displace a useful one and hurt the final combat score.

details.cap: Maximum 4 stacked help bonuses (e.g. 4x Chenko = +25% total in Bear Hunt; adding a 5th identical hero adds nothing).
details.displacement_rule: Selection is by hero strength (stars/power). A stronger hero takes one of the 4 slots even if its expedition buff is irrelevant to the fight.
details.example: 4x Chenko (4*) + 1x Seth (5*, blue): Seth is stronger, so it takes a slot from a Chenko — but Seth's buff is GATHERING, not damage, so it lowers the combat rally score.
details.implication: Keep your strongest usable heroes aligned to the fight type; a powerful hero with an off-type buff is a liability in that rally. Ties into which heroes to invest in (see planner/strategies.json -> rally-joiner-build-priority).

open_questions: Join-rally flow and formation selection (UI to map).
RESOLVED: the help/member bonus caps at 4 heroes; a stronger off-type hero can displace a useful one (see help-bonus-stacking-cap).
